comparison.objective: Sharpen both faces of a kitchen knife on a whetstone and return it safely to the chopping block.
comparison.physical_skill: Maintain a 13–22° bevel angle and near-level blade while making edge-leading heel-to-tip abrasive strokes, reorienting for both faces and safely releasing the knife.
comparison.success_condition: Later versions require ten qualifying strokes and coverage of at least 12 of 16 edge points per face in simulation, or measured sharpness at three of four points in reality, plus a stable edge-away put-down for full score. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparison.reason: Although both tasks regulate an angle, knife sharpening tests sustained abrasive contact, stroke direction and full-edge coverage rather than setting and mechanically locking an articulated stop against tightening reaction.
